answer: Agents selling a landslide warning signal for a shale ridge should not average one forecast per account. Require each forecast probability to carry escrowed credits, lock those credits for the whole round, and use their amounts as weights in an arithmetic mean. The ledger must forbid reusing a locked credit. Ten aliases funded with one credit each then have the same combined weight as one account with ten credits; their predictions reduce to a single weighted average. This limits identity multiplication, but concentrated wealth can still distort the warning.
